title: VLM auto-labeling harness for quad-layout patches
description: 'Endpoint to drive auto labeling of patches via vlm.' Python-side harness in ixdar_automation_cli (new module vlm_labeling.py + `ixdar-cli label-patches --ontology ontology.json [--patches ...] [--views 4]`) that, for each patch: calls /mesh/patches/focus and /mesh/patches/highlight (exclusive, high-contrast), captures `multiview` (or N single screenshots), sends the images plus the seeded label ontology and the neighbours' current labels to a vision-capable Claude model through the official anthropic Python SDK (model claude-opus-5, adaptive thinking, base64 image blocks, structured output for {labels:[...], new_categories:[...], confidence}), votes across views, and writes the result via /mesh/patches/label. Follows the SAMPart3D / Set-of-Mark pattern from the Labeling Mesh Patches note: highlighted region + multi-view + neighbour context for tiny patches; new categories are proposed, not silently created, and are written to a review file. Batch mode uses the Message Batches API for cost. Emit an agreement report against any hand-labelled patches present. Prior art to reuse: PATCH-10 (chunked Claude-CLI labeling for >50 patches on the semantic-patch decomposer) and the Daud voyage harness (VOYAGE-4 tournament selection with VLM, VOYAGE-19 VLM-labeled skeleton segments, VOYAGE-51 semantic patch decomposition of reference meshes; /home/acw/Code/Daud). Reuse their prompt/harness code where it fits; the target here is quad-layout patches, not curvature patches.
definition-of-done: 1. `ixdar-cli label-patches` labels every unlabelled patch of a saved layout in one run and persists via the API. 2. Ontology file format documented; proposed new categories land in a review JSON, not in the label store. 3. Multi-view voting implemented with a confidence threshold; low-confidence patches listed in the report. 4. Agreement report (per-label precision/recall) printed when hand labels exist. 5. API key comes from the environment (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or `ant auth login`); never from a flag or file in the repo. 6. Dry-run mode renders and saves the prompts/images without calling the API.
testing-plan: 1. Dry-run on the saved plane layout: 4 patches, verify 4 image sets and prompt JSON are produced. 2. Live run on a hand-labelled fixture (a saved layout of hand.dsl with ~20 patches labelled by hand): agreement >= 80% on top-level labels. 3. Batch mode run on the same fixture completes and produces identical labels to the sync path. 4. pytest for voting and report functions with canned model outputs.
todos: Add anthropic dependency to pyproject; client construction from env
Prompt builder: ontology + neighbour labels + highlighted multiview images
Structured-output schema for label proposals; parse with the SDK's parse helper
Voting across views; confidence threshold; review file for new categories
Batch API path for whole-model runs
Agreement report; dry-run mode; pytest coverage
unknowns: Whether single-patch granularity is too fine for the model on 284+ patch layouts; may need label propagation to patch groups first
Image budget per patch (views x resolution) vs cost; multiview 4x2 grid vs separate images
Which model tier is enough: start with claude-opus-5 per project default, measure agreement, only then consider cheaper models
